program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: A reflected expression orients the duplicating successor on the free recursor if and only if it is payload-blind with strict counter response, and all 76 method families close with native witnesses.
summary: The free recursor has terms built from zero, successor, wrapper and recursor with two root rules and their contextual closure. The question is which measures orient the duplicating successor rule that copies the payload into a wrapper. The main result is that a reflected scalar expression orients all successor instances exactly when it is payload-blind with strict counter response, independently of carrier. The coupled polynomial with parameters alpha and beta orients both rules exactly in the region alpha at least one and beta at least two, giving contextual termination witnessed at one and two. Growth analysis places each measure in a wrapper-cost versus gain cell, with the unbounded-cost bounded-gain cell excluding orientation and all other cells containing both verdicts. All seventy-six method families receive native witnesses satisfying laws and results with exact coverage and per-row hypothesis necessity counts.
boundary: On the orienting side, payload-blind counter-strict measures decrease from wrapped recursive call to successor instance at every carrier. On the failing side, payload-reading or counter-non-strict measures admit a concrete failed instance, and barrier-cell measures with unbounded wrapper cost and bounded gain admit no uniform orientation. The obstruction is the payload count growing from one to two with wrapper cost outrunning counter gain, located by the set equality between orienters and payload-blind counter-strict expressions together with the barrier-cell exclusion.

conclusions.statement: For every variable type and every reflected scalar measure expression, the profile measure decreases across every successor instance from wrapped recursive call to successor instance if and only if the expression is payload-blind and counter-strict.
For every variable type, the set of expressions orienting every successor instance equals the set of payload-blind counter-strict expressions.
For every method family, there exists data satisfying its laws and its row result on the free recursor.
The covered rows equal the full family list allMethodFamilies, with no hypotheses.
Both free recursor rules are oriented by the coupled interpretation if and only if 1 is at most alpha and 2 is at most beta.
For every variable type, reverse contextual rewriting on free terms is well-founded.
For every schema and measure, unbounded wrapper margin together with bounded counter gain at a base-counter pair excludes strict orientation at that pair for all payloads.
If a measure retains wrappers at a cost, has a uniform gain bound and has unbounded values then it does not orient all duplicating instances.
If a measure retains both wrapper arguments at a cost and orients every duplicating instance then for all base, payload and counter the payload value plus the cost is below counter gain.
For every schema, measure and duplicating instance, orientation at that instance holds if and only if wrapper cost is below counter gain.
For every schema, measure and fixed base and counter, the measure lies in one of the four bounded versus unbounded wrapper and gain combinations.
The six witnesses show all three non-barrier cells contain both an orienter and a non-orienter.
For every index below the certificates length, the family list after erasing that certificate differs from the full family list.
Filtered catalog lengths are 16 deleted premises, 5 law-free controls, 42 deleted features and 13 with no hypothesis.
If an m-step contextual derivation from t to u holds then m plus 2 is at most 3 to the termSize of t.

openPoints: Counter-admissibility is carried as a hypothesis for the variant where successor orientation reduces to payload-blindness.

Minimal-chain soundness carries decidable equality of variables and the condition that right-hand variables occur on the left; the system with rule c to a fresh variable shows empty well-founded chains without termination.

Polynomial, multilinear, cross-term and coupling barriers carry dominance, bounded-gain and unbounded-value premises such as frozen base dominance, absence of counter exponent or step-counter coupling, and eventual dominance.

Matrix, tuple and interpretation lifts carry positivity premises such as wrapper coefficients at least one, diagonal at least one, positive margin, floor structure, affine first-projection shape and strict context laws.
Sorted, context-sensitive and persistence transfers carry replacement-map activity, conservativeness, Zantema side condition and inhabitance; usable-chain transfer is limited to usable-rooted calls.

The residual successor decision at slope at least two is left open and encodes bivariate positivity; completeness is shown on monotone, univariate, base-affine, payload-affine and monomial-difference strata with extracted failing witnesses.

Infinitary convergence needs an unbounded depth schedule, quasi-interpretation bounds need a paired reduction order for termination, and sharing and quotient transfers do not conserve normal forms, step counts or the converse direction.

files.summary: This file defines counter depth, matched and recursive counters, the strict-subterm relation and admittance predicates for ten ledger rows. It proves the recursive call is the strict predecessor with smaller depth and that the subterm relation is well founded. It anchors five admittance rows for HORPO, CPO, general schema, sized types and Coq guard, two typing-barrier rows for linear logic and ramified recursion, and abstraction, size-change and infinitary rows.
files.conclusion: Every structural-descent definitional criterion admits the duplicating recursor, while no resource-sound linear or ramified typing admits it, and the full contextual relation is well founded with no infinite reduction.

files.summary: This file defines affine, truncated, max, bounded polynomial, multilinear, natural and ordered-field matrix, arctic and tropical, triangular, tuple and Archimedean measures with fourteen row claims. It proves none of those classes orient the duplicating step under the stated dominance, monotonicity or projection premises. It compiles cross-coupled orienting witnesses showing the premises are load-bearing and that the certificate-free tropical strengthening is false.
files.conclusion: No member of the listed algebraic classes orients the duplicating step, with dominance and affine-projection premises proved load-bearing by explicit orienting counterexamples.

files.summary: This file defines the counter-projection core, reduction pairs and triples, formative and neutral processors, typed and order-sorted transports, context-sensitive closures, rule-schema catalogs and constrained encodings. It proves the single extracted pair decreases in counter depth and discharges every dependency-pair row. It proves unconditionality collapses conditional and two-dimensional notions and that no Bellantoni-Cook tier assignment is admissible.
files.conclusion: The single counter-decreasing dependency pair discharges all dependency-pair and typed rows and conditional variants collapse to the unconditional case, while no Bellantoni-Cook tier assignment can accommodate the duplicating rule.

files.summary: This file defines the generic diagonal-fork schema, its smallest three-element inhabitant and three extension predicates for equality query, injective pairing and infinite carrier. It proves the tiny fork lacks all three, so the bare schema forces none of them. It proves KO7 traces supply infinite generation and injective merge pairing while the guarded relation supplies the parameterized equality query, combined in one fence theorem.
files.conclusion: The generic diagonal-fork schema does not force equality, pairing or infinity, while KO7 realizes all three, as recorded once in the fence theorem.

files.summary: This file defines six closed singleton carriers for counter-only filtering, neutral processing, single-call size-change, guarded Cichon bounds, merge-commutativity quotient and shared-node substrate. It proves each inhabitant equals the existing KO7 object and satisfies an exact certificate with load-bearing graph, rank and nonconservativity facts. It proves filtering and size-change ranks coincide as functions with the common dependency-pair confession core.
files.conclusion: Every closed exact carrier is the concrete KO7 method and satisfies its certificate, with filtering and size-change ranks equal to the common dependency-pair projection.

files.summary: This file defines natural matrix actions, weak-strict vector orders, matrix operations and natural and triangular method structures with published monotonicity laws. It proves strictness is equivalent to a positive diagonal and that the order is well founded and compatible. It proves no such method orients the duplicating step, with explicit nonconstant size instances.
files.conclusion: No EWZ-monotone natural or triangular matrix interpretation orients the duplicating schema step.

files.summary: This file defines delta-margin comparison, field matrix operations and ordered matrix methods with genuinely field coefficients. It proves margin preservation is equivalent to a diagonal of at least one and well-foundedness via natural floor. It proves no such method orients the duplicating step, with scaled size and fractional instances showing genuine field use.
files.conclusion: No ordered-field matrix interpretation with the stated monotonicity orients the duplicating step over the rationals or reals.

files.summary: This file studies two ablations of the step-duplicating free syntax. It defines tree size and a non-duplicating recursor rule, proving tree size strictly decreases and its reverse is well founded. It defines a payload-blind counter projection that orients the original duplicating successor yet fails wrapper left-sensitivity. The final theorem packages the independence of payload duplication and payload sensitivity.
files.conclusion: Payload duplication and payload sensitivity are independent obligations, with size descent available only after removing duplication and orientation available from a payload-blind counter that is not wrapper-sensitive.

files.summary: This file builds concrete native interpretations for the algebraic rows previously stated only as row propositions. It defines truncated-debt, max, bounded-polynomial, multilinear, ordered-field matrix, higher-order tuple, Archimedean and finite Arctic measures with non-triviality controls. Each concrete method is shown to be blocked from uniform duplicator orientation by the corresponding universal barrier. Two-sided polynomial and multilinear boundary witnesses pair an inside member with a cross-coupled orienter outside, and all data are packaged in a capstone bundle.
files.conclusion: All ten algebraic rows receive concrete native method data with activeness controls, universal barriers blocking uniform orientation, and a capstone bundle pairing each blocked inhabitant with its boundary escape where one exists.

files.summary: This file defines counter and payload observations and closed towers realizing every natural value. It proves every counter, payload and positive increment occurs as an actual successor root step at every variable type via a closed embedding that preserves both observations and root steps. Orientation of successors by a profile is then equivalent to the numeric duplicating-step condition, hence carrier-independent, with payload blindness as a consequence.
files.conclusion: Every counter, payload and positive increment occurs as a successor profile at every carrier, so successor orientation is equivalent to the numeric duplicating-step condition and is carrier-independent.

files.summary: This file defines a total capture-avoiding substitution for the named higher-order syntax. It introduces free variables, all names, maxima, depth, bound renaming and fresh-name generation with correctness lemmas. Fuel recursion with alpha-renaming of conflicting binders yields the public operation, certified by an explicit derivation relation. Concrete controls contrast the legacy capturing substitution with the renaming, shadowing and preservation behavior of the new operation.
files.conclusion: Every call to capture-avoiding substitution carries a capture-avoidance derivation, and the controls show it renames conflicting binders instead of capturing.

files.summary: This file splits every natural-valued interpretation at fixed base and counter by boundedness of wrapper margin and counter gain. It proves the dichotomies, four-cell coverage, and that the unbounded-wrapper and bounded-gain cell excludes orientation. On the free schema it exhibits a counter orienter and zero non-orienter in the bounded and bounded cell, coupled and doubled-wrapper witnesses in the unbounded and unbounded cell, and bounded-wrapper and alternating-gain witnesses for the bounded and unbounded cell, packaged as a catalog showing each non-barrier cell has both verdicts.
files.conclusion: The barrier cell excludes orientation and every non-barrier cell contains both an orienter and a non-orienter.

files.summary: This file places each direct barrier family in the wrapper and gain growth cells at the base pair. It proves retention, threshold and dominance lemmas showing additive, affine, quadratic, max, compositional, cross-term, multilinear and polynomial measures lie in the barrier cell or fail past a threshold, and derives each family barrier from the cell theorem. Vector families are reduced to their tracked affine scalar, and the scalar grammar is characterized through cells on the free schema.
files.conclusion: All direct families are recovered as cell corollaries lying in the barrier cell or failing pointwise, and grammar orientation is equivalent to absence of barrier cells plus counter strictness.

files.summary: This file states regression controls for certificates, extraction, connectors, size-change graphs, neutral processors and pair chains. It checks that certificates store canonical interpretations and are unique, that erasing one row breaks sixty-row coverage, and that extraction returns the recursive call occurring in the true right-hand side but rejects altered payloads and call-as-rhs. It also checks resetting connectors defeat chain well-foundedness, strictness only at the counter coordinate, rejection of empty neutral outputs, and that pair-chain well-foundedness does not imply source termination.
files.conclusion: Mutation controls pin canonical certificates, extraction correctness, coordinate strictness, neutrality, and the separation between pair-chain well-foundedness and source termination.

files.summary: The file defines four certificate kinds for termination of the free recursor, namely polynomial, matrix, Knuth-Bendix and dependency-pair certificates, with an executable checker that dispatches to kind-specific decision procedures. For polynomials it proves soundness and, under the positive linear monomial test, completeness for root orientation, and on the multilinear class equivalence between acceptance, root orientation and strict monotonicity in every argument. It proves that no retentive affine polynomial, matrix or Knuth-Bendix certificate is accepted, while the counter-projection dependency-pair certificate and a coupled polynomial certificate are accepted. The Knuth-Bendix and dependency-pair checkers are proved sound and complete for their orders and criteria, and a final boundary theorem conjoins the rejections, acceptances, soundness and equivalences.
files.conclusion: Every accepted certificate proves termination, yet no retentive affine, matrix or Knuth-Bendix certificate is ever accepted while the coupled polynomial and counter-projection certificates are.

files.summary: The file defines orientation of the free contextual closure and proves that any contextual orienter restricts to a root orienter. It proves that measures in the barrier cell with unbounded wrapper cost and bounded counter gain cannot orient the context closure, and that tree size lies in that cell at every pair so it never orients contexts. In the positive direction it shows strict context laws lift root orientation to contextual decrease and to well-foundedness of the reverse contextual relation. Two controls separate the premises: a minimum-wrapper interpretation orients both root rules but fails context orientation, and a zero-step simulation does not transfer termination.
files.conclusion: Strict context laws lift root orientation to contextual termination, while barrier-cell measures and the minimum-wrapper interpretation show root orientation alone does not imply contextual orientation.

files.summary: The file collects standalone controls: the singleton schema where the duplicating rule is a self-loop no measure orients, scalar-grammar classifications including payload-reading products, payload-blind zero multiples and orienting counter recodings, and a rational shrinking measure that decreases along a nonterminating step while a separated comparison on nonnegative rationals is well founded. It shows adding a self-loop keeps every coupling barrier but loses termination, dropping the duplicating rule for a linear successor rule admits an orienting size measure meeting all barrier hypotheses, and the same linear certificate fails after altering the source rule. It also exhibits a well-founded fan with arbitrarily long finite branches and no natural rank, and the empty system with empty dependency-pair problem and termination.
files.conclusion: The controls isolate each hypothesis by showing rational decrease, well-foundedness, barriers and certificates do not survive the corresponding weakening or extension.

files.summary: The file gives the cell form of the coupling corollary: a wrapper-retentive orienter with unbounded payload values lies in the unbounded-wrapper unbounded-gain cell. It defines the counter projection that drops the wrapper payload and an affine recursive-drop measure with zero recursive-result coefficient, computing wrapper cost zero and minus counter value respectively and counter gain one for both. Both measures orient every successor instance, fail retention at every cost, and violate the coupled gain inequality, providing expected-negative controls for each half of the retention premise.
files.conclusion: Both the counter projection and the recursive-drop measure orient all successor instances while failing retention at every cost.

files.summary: The file defines integer wrapper cost and counter gain for natural-valued interpretations and proves pointwise and uniform equivalences between orientation of the duplicating rule and cost below gain. It proves that wrapper retention plus orientation forces counter gain above the retained payload value, so bounded gain with unbounded payload precludes orientation. It reuses the unconstrained direct-law barrier as the bounded-gain corollary and computes the exact gain of the polynomial witness with its tight coupling margin.
files.conclusion: Retention with bounded gain and unbounded payload makes orientation impossible, with the polynomial witness attaining the bound tightly.

files.summary: The file defines same-system dependency-pair problems, native reduction pairs and triples with explicit weak and strict relations, and a source lexicographic bridge for recovering source termination. It gives polynomial and gap-two reduction pairs with different strict relations, proves every native pair certifies well-foundedness of the pair problem, and shows pair well-foundedness alone does not imply source termination via a pair-free self-loop. It adds fixture conditions, a two-dimensional pair relation, constrained certificates and higher-order substitution controls, packaged in a concrete native bundle.
files.conclusion: Native pairs certify pair well-foundedness, but source termination needs the separate lexicographic bridge, as the pair-free self-loop shows.

files.summary: Defines strongly normalizing terms, single-argument rewrite steps, defined symbols, subterms, minimal dependency-chain steps between calls, call reduction pairs and the subterm criterion with a call projection for finite first-order rewrite systems. Proves that well-foundedness of the minimal chain relation implies every term is strongly normalizing under the condition that right-hand-side variables occur in the left-hand side, and derives termination from a call reduction pair and from the subterm criterion. Shows the variable condition is necessary through the one-rule system c -> x, which has an empty hence well-founded chain relation but loops. Instantiates the criterion on a free recursor with zero and successor rules, proving termination by the counter projection and that wrapper-rooted pairs are not chain steps.
files.conclusion: Well-founded minimal dependency chains imply termination under the variable condition, with reduction-pair and subterm criteria as consequences, and the condition is sharp as shown by c -> x.

files.summary: Defines package law structures ORI1Laws through ORI6Laws that restate blocked, well-foundedness and orientation facts about the stored native interpretation objects for path orders, algebraic interpretations, semantic-structural methods, dependency-pair methods, higher-order methods and substrate-change methods. Defines the row-indexed predicates NativeMethodLaws and NativeRowWitness that attach to each MissingNativeInterpretation constructor the laws and witness about its exact stored package object, and the DependentNativeCertificate structure pairing an interpretation with both. Proves every row-indexed interpretation satisfies its laws and witness, and that the canonical dependent certificates select the same sixty method families as the native interpretation layer with exactly sixty rows. Shows membership in those rows yields a certificate whose laws speak about its own stored interpretation.
files.conclusion: Exactly sixty method families carry interpretation-dependent certificates whose laws and row witnesses speak about their own stored interpretation.

files.summary: The file enumerates fourteen direct barrier families and their 27 load-bearing hypothesis slots, with carriers that delete exactly one premise and specifications of the deleted premise and excluded orientation. It constructs explicit orienting valuations (counter and step weights, negative and retention-failing additive measures, unbalanced mixed-coordinate and zero-weight functional models, among others) showing each barrier fails without its premise, and proves that restoring the premise restores the live barrier by calling that family's barrier theorem. It also proves joint and auxiliary redundancies: both wrapper coefficients together and several successor, recursor and wrapper-weight fields are not load-bearing. Finally it shows both hypotheses of the barrier cell are individually necessary by independent countermodels.
files.conclusion: Every one of the 27 load-bearing premises across the fourteen direct barrier families is exactly necessary: restoring it restores the orientation barrier, and deleting it admits an explicit orienting countermodel.

files.summary: This file factors the method data of six singleton exact promotion carriers into carrier-parametric interfaces for argument filtering, neutral processors, size-change, Cichon descent, equational quotients and sharing. Each interface stores its operations and laws, and a concrete KO7 instance is shown to recover the exact promoted rank, relation or functions. The capstone theorem assembles all six recoveries while the other ten historical rows keep their carrier-wide statements.
files.conclusion: All six exact historical promotion carriers are recovered as instances of generic carrier-parametric method interfaces.

files.summary: This file defines term size and a polynomial weight for the free two-rule recursor and proves the weight drops on every root and contextual step. It derives an upper bound of fewer than 3 to the term size steps for any derivation and a matching exponential lower bound from a nested payload family that emits and reduces k copies per level. A final dependency-pair escape counts recursive calls by the drop of the successor counter.
files.conclusion: Every contextual derivation from t has fewer than 3 to the size of t steps and the nested family shows this single-exponential bound is essentially tight.

files.summary: This file bounds ordinal heights by natural-valued decreasing functions and shows heights of a well-founded relation form an initial segment. Applied to the free recursor, both the reversed contextual relation and the reversed recursive-call relation have heights exactly the natural numbers with supremum omega. A four-symbol path order with a Veblen ranking orients both root rules, decreases on every comparison, stays below veblen 4 0 and is cofinal there.
files.conclusion: Both the contextual and call heights attain exactly all natural numbers with supremum omega, while the MPO ranking is cofinal in veblen 4 0.

files.summary: This file defines a coupled polynomial interpretation with parameters alpha and beta and proves the whole region alpha at least 1 and beta at least 2 orients both recursor rules. It proves strict monotonicity in every constructor argument and lifts root orientation to a strict decrease on every one-hole contextual step. The generic transfer then yields strong normalization of full contextual rewriting, with alpha 1 beta 2 as a concrete witness, and root rewriting follows as a subrelation.
files.conclusion: Every interpretation with alpha at least 1 and beta at least 2 proves strong normalization of the full contextual free recursor, in particular alpha 1 beta 2.

files.summary: This file translates between payload-blindness and not using the payload and between adequacy and orientation, showing the grammar theorem and the direct-grammar license are the same statement. It proves the license criterion and the equivalence of separation with the payload half of the grammar theorem. It also shows every denotation-preserving self-map preserves both predicates, with sum-commutation as a non-identity example, and records what aggregations of recursive arguments can use.
files.conclusion: Grammar orientation and the operational-inexpressibility license are the same statement under identity translation, which is not unique.

files.summary: This file gives native higher-order syntax with a well-founded proper-subterm relation and matched and recursive counters. It defines a specialized HORPO fragment and a computability-closure fragment, both admitting the decreasing call, plus general schema calls, guard derivations, sized calls, safe-normal and ramified derivations, resource typing and abstract interpretation. Positive controls accept identity and the decreasing call while reversed, equal-index and duplicating rules are rejected, and finite rewriting is separated from an infinite loop in a final bundle.
files.conclusion: The displayed decreasing recursive call is admitted by HORPO, computability closure, guard, sized and resource methods while duplicating and nondecreasing variants are rejected.

files.summary: This file defines evidence carriers for hypothesis necessity with four row classes. Barrier rows use deleted-premise countermodels and retained-premise refutations, including law-free, universal and covered variants without a removable premise. Escape rows use feature lenses and accepted-to-rejected change controls, while rows with no applicable hypothesis use a laws-determine-verdict reason that rules out any feature control.
files.conclusion: Necessity evidence is classified into deleted premise, law-free and universal and covered barriers, defining-feature change, or no applicable hypothesis.

files.summary: This file proves datatype-independent arithmetic for wrapper costs and recursor increments, including Nat and ordered-group orientation equivalences and accumulation of one-step margins across iterates via linear and affine geometric sums. A general no-go shows bounded increments conflict with unbounded attained costs for uniform orientation. Explicit controls separate truncated Nat subtraction from integer differences and separate bounded-cost, coupled-increment and collapsed-payload cases.
files.conclusion: Uniform orientation fails under bounded increments with unbounded costs, while one-step margins accumulate linearly and affinely and Nat subtraction needs an integer lift.

files.summary: This file defines generic interpretations of the four free constructors with evaluation and a substitution commutation lemma. It defines strict and weak constructor laws and algebraic orientation of the two root rules. Root orientation plus strict laws is shown to decrease every contextual step and to transfer well-foundedness to reverse contextual rewriting, stably under substitution.
files.conclusion: Root orientation plus strict constructor monotonicity lifts to full contextual decrease and well-foundedness, stably under substitution.

files.summary: This file states a single bridge theorem collecting the confession and distinction license event on the free recursor. It conjoins counter adequacy and payload blindness, deterministic role-channel equalities with entropy deficit and one-bit exchange, and observer sufficiency via kernel refinement with call-counter decrease. The recorded relations are channel equality and shared kernel refinement rather than separate bounds.
files.conclusion: Counter orientation, payload-blindness license, rary channel equalities with entropy deficit, observer kernel characterization and call-rank decrease hold together as one license event.

files.summary: This file exposes the dependent-evidence layer under audit names for method data, laws and result about the same stored object. It proves the factoring coherent and restates dependent coverage in factored form. The factored layer covers exactly sixty complementary rows with the same row list as the native-interpretation layer.
files.conclusion: Every one of the 60 dependent rows carries data whose laws and witness concern that same data.

files.summary: This file assigns every row of the method universe one necessity class, one statement from its own laws and acceptance, and one proof calling its own theorem. The catalog rows are exactly the live method universe with length 76, no duplicates and full coverage. Rows split into 16 deleted premises, 5 law-free controls, 42 deleted features and 13 with no applicable hypothesis.
files.conclusion: All 76 method families satisfy their assigned necessity statement, split 16, 5, 42 and 13 across the four necessity classes.

files.summary: This file formalizes four method rows for conditional and constrained rewriting around a conditional recursor and its integer and constrained analogues. It defines conditional rewriting as an inference system with goal stacks and proof trees, 2D dependency pairs with minimal chains, the unraveling U(R), integer rewriting with innermost predefined steps, and logically constrained rewriting with calculation steps. It proves soundness of the 2D removal triple, of unraveling termination via a marked algebra, of the integer conditional reduction pair with a bound, and of the LCTRS value criterion, each with a concrete witness, liveness features, and mutations that break acceptance.
files.conclusion: The four witnesses satisfy their laws and acceptance and thereby establish operational termination or innermost termination for the conditional recursor, its unraveling, the integer recursor, and the constrained recursor, while the mutations show the strictness and bound conditions are necessary.

files.summary: This file formalises seven dependency-pair processor rows for the free recursor. It defines linear interpretations on calls, weak and strict decrease conditions, reduction pairs and triples, argument filterings, neutral processors, processor sequences, and size-change graphs from dependency pairs. Each row proves a soundness theorem that lawful accepting data imply termination, exhibits a concrete witness, and exhibits mutations where blinding, retaining, erasing or deleting break laws, acceptance or termination.
files.conclusion: Seven dependency-pair processor rows each certify termination of the free recursor with an explicit witness, and each is shown tight by mutations that break laws, acceptance or termination.

files.summary: This file formalises three graph-calculi method rows for the free recursor translated to graph rewriting. It defines hypergraphs, type graphs, weight algebras, graph weights as minima over typings, and sharing-aware assignments with read-back to closed terms. Each row proves soundness for termination or a reachable size bound, gives a two-node witness separating sharing the one-node flower cannot, and shows mutations and scope limits where zero weights, arbitrary gluing or weak inequalities alone fail.
files.conclusion: Weighted, generalized weighted and sharing-aware rows certify the free recursor graph translation with explicit two-node witnesses, while zero and constant weights, unglued contexts and unpaired quasi-interpretations are shown insufficient for termination.

files.summary: The file formalizes fifteen method rows for orientation of the free duplicating rule recur b s (succ n) to wrap s (recur b s n). It defines rule orientation, free-termination certification, bridges to P3 barrier cells, and for each method its data, admissibility laws, acceptance and barrier or escape verdict. It proves universal barriers for linear, matrix, triangular, arctic, tropical, affine-tuple and finite members and exhibits coupled witnesses for negative-coefficient, max, higher-degree, multilinear, tuple and monotone-algebra methods, each with mutation and signature-lifting controls.
files.conclusion: The file establishes the fifteen-row classification in which lawful linear, matrix, arctic, tropical and finite members are barred from orienting the duplicating rule while the exhibited coupled witnesses orient it and certify termination, with each verdict lifting to arbitrary signatures.

files.summary: This file defines a shared first-order KBO core with weighted evaluation, variable counts, lexicographic and Huet-Oppen multiset clauses, and proves it a reduction order on well-formed terms. It also defines the generalized KBO over weakly monotone strictly simple algebras with the same reduction-order properties. It instantiates eight method rows over the free recursor schema and proves barriers for standard, subterm-coefficient, status, transfinite, lambda-free and AC variants while the generalized and polynomial witnesses orient both free rules and yield termination.
files.conclusion: The shared first-order and generalized KBO cores are reduction orders, six KBO variants are uniformly barred from the duplicating rule by the variable condition, and generalized and polynomial KBOs escape the barrier and terminate the free recursor.

files.summary: This file formalizes nine method rows for the free recursor and free schema: semantic, root, self-labelling and quasi-decreasingness over first-order terms, and match-bound, raise-consistency, left-linear, predictive-labelling and forward-closure rows over raised terms. It defines algebras, labelled terms, flat-context closure, quotient and root algebras, conditional rewriting with quasi-decreasing orders, and raised height certificates. It proves soundness and transfer theorems showing the labelling, raise-consistency, predictive and quasi-decreasingness witnesses terminate the free systems. It proves universal barrier theorems showing no linear match-bound, left-linear or right-linear forward-closure certificate can certify the duplicating system, including a terminating conditional system that is not quasi-decreasing.
files.conclusion: Semantic, root, self and predictive labelling with raise-consistency and quasi-decreasingness certify termination of the free recursor and schema, while no linear match-bound, left-linear or right-linear forward-closure certificate can certify the duplicating system and conditional termination does not imply quasi-decreasingness.

files.summary: This file implements two orientation-closure method rows for other calculi. The first formalizes infinitary rewriting with depth truncations, coherent infinite-term presentations, a duplicating stage family converging to an infinite wrap tower, and a soundness theorem from unbounded certified depths to convergence. The second formalizes native higher-order cost-size tuple interpretations with a coupled iterator cost, proves strict cost decrease for the free rules and contexts, and supplies a unit-coefficient witness proving termination of free contextual rewriting.
files.conclusion: Finite contextual rewriting terminates while the infinitary duplicator admits a strongly convergent infinite reduction, and the coupled higher-order tuple witness proves termination of the free contextual relation at every variable type.

files.summary: The file defines the recursive path order with multiset and lexicographic status, its Dershowitz-Manna extension, and its quotient by permutative congruence, proving well-foundedness, stability, monotonicity and termination soundness. It defines the polynomial path order POP* and proves containment in the multiset path order, hence irreflexivity, well-foundedness and termination, plus an exact acceptance characterization for the free recursor. It instantiates five method rows on the free two-rule system with soundness theorems, witnesses, acceptance equivalences and mutations, and proves POP* is not transitive, not context-closed, not substitution-closed, with linear innermost scope but exponential derivational complexity.
files.conclusion: The recursive, permutative, polynomial, AC and simplification orders all orient the free two-rule recursor and prove termination of its contextual relation, while POP* provably fails transitivity, context closure, substitution closure and derivational-complexity extension.

files.summary: The file defines a finite synchronous pi-calculus fragment with processes, communication steps, sender/receiver sessions, and a counter encoding with its depth measure, proving each step decreases size or depth and is well-founded. It implements the pi-calculus termination-translation row as level/data certificates with laws, acceptance, verdict, witness, mutation and scope, plus a carrier-independent termination-reflecting translation used for global countdown simulations. It defines erasing-head lambda-mu terms, beta contraction, size and a continuation-passing translation, implementing the lambda-mu strong-normalisation row with the same P5 contract and a rank into natural-number descent. Soundness, scope and method-identity theorems discharge both rows and state the exact translation principles used.
files.conclusion: Both the synchronous process counter simulation and the erasing-head lambda-mu CPS rank yield well-founded relations, with fully proved scopes and exact method identities.

files.summary: The file implements three semantic-framework rows for the free recursor: an abstract-interpretation ranking abstraction with simulation and rank decrease, a powerset-coalgebra categorical row with morphism laws and no-infinite-path verdicts, and a higher-order constrained rewriting row with projection laws and the value criterion. Each row provides data, laws, acceptance, verdict, witness, mutation or loop counterexample, scope and method-identity theorems, with soundness proved via coupled polynomial interpretation, accessibility, and constrained dependency-pair chains. A generic ranking-abstraction theorem, Taylor well-founded coalgebra lemmas, and the applicative higher-order recursor with its constraint semantics support the three instances.
files.conclusion: Ranking abstractions, well-founded powerset coalgebras, and the higher-order value criterion each prove termination of their free-system instances with fully proved arbitrary-carrier scopes.

files.summary: The file builds restricted rewriting with admitted substitutions and active positions, its minimal chains, chain soundness and subterm criterion. It instantiates this to context-sensitive rewriting with a replacement map, to many-sorted type introduction with Zantema's condition and the Toyama system, to order-sorted rewriting, and to a layered many-sorted persistence proof with projections and principal subterms. Each row has laws, an acceptance criterion, a soundness theorem, a concrete witness for the free recursor, feature examples and mutations showing the hypotheses are necessary.
files.conclusion: The free recursor terminates unsorted via the native two-sort many-sorted witness, and more generally rule-typed sorted termination is equivalent to unsorted termination.

files.summary: The file defines string and cycle rewriting on words, rewriting modulo finite equations, and maximally shared term-graph rewriting, all applied to the free recursor with free terms, contexts and steps imported from earlier files. It proves bounded length growth for finite string and cycle systems and a general encoding barrier saying no bounded-growth word relation performs every ground duplicating recursor step under compositional-length encodings. It packages four method rows with universal barrier or transfer theorems, concrete witnesses including the 01 to 10 rule, commutativity of wrap, a cost-doubling shared step and the Toyama system, and mutations with degenerate empty encoding, looping ground equation and stutter policy showing sharpness. It also proves transfers from cycle to string termination and from modulo and sharing termination to free termination, while exhibiting non-conservation of normal forms, step counts and the converse termination direction.
files.conclusion: No finite compositional-length string or cycle system performs the duplicating recursor step in one step, and quotient and sharing termination transfer to free terms without conserving normal forms, step counts or the converse direction.

files.summary: The file defines simply typed applicative terms over System T sorts, typed signatures, applicative rewriting, and the typed iterator and Godel recursor rules with an adapter from the free first-order schema. It formalises four typed termination methods: the higher-order recursive path ordering, the computability path ordering, the general-schema computable closure, and sized types, each with clauses, acceptance, laws, witness and soundness statements. Each row is proved sound by embedding its clauses into the recursive path order with application minimal, yielding termination of the typed iterator rules and by transfer of the free schema. It also proves that all four methods admit Godels recursor rules and hence terminate System T recursor rewriting.
files.conclusion: All four typed methods admit Godels System T recursor rules and yield termination of recursor rewriting, hence of the typed iterator rules and of the free schema.

files.summary: This file formalizes four typing disciplines as method rows for the free recursor with base, payload and counter. It defines linear typing with exponentials, tiered ramified recurrence, Bellantoni-Cook safe recursion, and the Rocq guard condition with call-by-value evaluation. Each row proves soundness in the form of resource preservation, polynomial height or size bounds, or termination, and determines whether the duplicating successor rule is admitted. Witnesses, mutations that flip each side condition, and scope statements delimit the omitted material for every row.
files.conclusion: The file proves that exponential-free linear typing rejects the duplicating recursor while tiered, safe-normal and guarded disciplines admit it with polynomial bounds or termination under sharp side conditions.

files.summary: This file formalizes usable-rules and formative-rules rows for dependency-pair problems over a generic first-order library. It defines the least usable symbol and rule sets generated from pair-target roots and proves closure, leastness, and replay of rewriting and chains inside the generated rules. For the free two-rule recursor the usable symbols collapse to the recursor while the duplicating rule is retained, yielding finiteness on usable-rooted calls. It then defines formative rule and pair catalogs selected from the actual eight-schema source and proves sufficiency, closure, exactness and well-foundedness.
files.conclusion: The file proves that the generated usable rules are the least closed set and carry chain finiteness to usable-rooted calls while retaining duplication, and that the selected formative catalog is exact and well-founded for the actual pair problem.

files.summary: The file defines statusAdmits, which records which closure verdicts each finer-table status allows. It proves that for each of the 76 termination method families, the status assigned by statusOf admits the verdict assigned by methodVerdict. It derives directional consequences for barrier and escape cases and shows that an escape-status row carries the orienting MethodResult proved by the closure table. It also records the statuses of seven named methods discussed in the paper methods table.
files.conclusion: For every one of the 76 methods, the finer-table status admits the closure-table verdict.

files.summary: The file unifies 76 termination-method catalogue rows over the free recursor. It defines per-family data, laws, acceptance and result predicates, a four-valued barrier-escape verdict, and uniform soundness, feature and mutation statements assembled from the row modules. It constructs a witness for each family and proves the witnesses satisfy the laws and results, the uniform soundness, feature and mutation theorems, and exact identity theorems for 13 repaired named methods. It packages witnesses as row certificates, shows the certificate list covers exactly the full family list, and shows deleting any certificate breaks coverage.
files.conclusion: Every one of the 76 method families has witness data satisfying its laws and its row result on the free recursor.

files.summary: This file binds each of the 76 RDRS method-family rows to method-native semantics. The sixteen rows already covered by the legacy evidence interface are assigned False and return none, while the other sixty rows receive exact row propositions, indexed interpretation objects, and proof-bearing evidence. It proves the interpretation list and evidence list both have length 60, coincide, are duplicate-free, and that the legacy list has length 16 and is disjoint. The capstone structure packages these counts and existence properties as closed coverage.
files.conclusion: The sixty non-legacy RDRS rows each have a native interpretation object and proof-bearing native proposition disjoint from the sixteen legacy rows, packaged as a closed coverage.

files.summary: This file defines observed steps, the reverse observed relation, factored ranks into arbitrary targets, exact-length paths, and natural-valued ranks. It proves a factored rank into a well-founded target yields well-foundedness of the reverse observed relation with a converse via the identity rank, and that natural ranks exist exactly under bounded heights. It gives a well-founded top countdown with no natural rank, a terminating two-chain whose identifying observation cycles with no factored rank, and a constant collapse with a self-loop.
files.conclusion: Well-foundedness lifts through an observer exactly when the reverse observed relation is well-founded, but natural-valued ranks need bounded heights and collapsing observations can destroy termination.

files.summary: This file defines when an observer licenses a well-founded rank and compares licensing observers with the counter of a counter system. It proves a counter-factored observer licenses exactly when the factoring map is injective, equivalently when kernels agree, and that observers sufficient for the counter are exactly kernel refinements with quotient isomorphic to Nat. On the free recursor call relation it builds two incomparable licensing observers whose common coarsenings license none, refuting a coarsest licensing observer, and shows fiber-constant ranks are strict recodings while arbitrary ranks have infinitely many orders.
files.conclusion: Counter-factored licensing is exactly injectivity while the free call relation has two incomparable licensing observers with no coarsest licensing observer and infinitely many rank orders without fiber constancy.

files.summary: This file presents the Orientation Boundary as a set of reflected grammar expressions with semantic and syntactic descriptions. It proves the set orienting all successor instances equals the payload-blind counter-strict set at every variable type, hence carrier-independently and in intersection over all types, with the counter inside and payload and constants outside. It defines four growth cells and proves every measure lies in some cell and at most one, with the barrier cell excluding uniform orientation.
files.conclusion: The set of expressions orienting all successor instances equals the payload-blind counter-strict set independently of carrier, and every measure lies in exactly one of four growth cells with the barrier cell excluding uniform orientation.

files.summary: This file packages paper-facing consequences of existing Orientation Boundary families without new measure language or decision problems. It proves the per-carrier equivalence between successor orientation and payload blindness with strict counter response, its all-carriers corollary, and the counter-admissible variant reducing to payload blindness. It also proves a payload-erasing step admits no decisive payload-sensitive certificate.
files.conclusion: Orientation of successor instances is exactly payload blindness plus strict counter response, and payload-erasing steps admit no decisive payload-sensitive certificate.

files.summary: This file collects the Orientation Boundary hypothesis-necessity results in one theorem. It covers the fourteen direct barrier families with twenty-seven consumed premises, deleted-premise countermodels, restore-and-refute pairs, and three empty-premise families. It also covers necessity of both barrier-cell growth hypotheses and necessity statements and kind counts for all seventy-six method rows.
files.conclusion: All fourteen barrier families with twenty-seven premises and all seventy-six method rows have exact necessity statements with the stated class counts.

files.summary: This file defines native path-order semantics for the ten ORI-1 rows with computations from method weights, precedence, status, AC theory, ordinal weights, applicative encoding, and polynomial functions. It proves each comparison carries the variable condition and is well-founded where claimed, with concrete witnesses including multiset status, collapsing precedence, ordinal weights, and nonlinear polynomials. It shows every variant blocks the duplicating schema rule and packages all rows with nontriviality controls into a concrete ORI-1 semantics.
files.conclusion: All ten ORI-1 path-order methods have native weight, precedence, status, AC, ordinal, applicative, and polynomial semantics that are well-founded where claimed yet uniformly block the duplicating rule.

files.summary: This file defines constructor-local natural-coefficient polynomial interpretations with monomial lists W and R and the predicates OrientsSucc and OrientsZero. It proves exact univariate orientation criteria for wrappers with y-coefficient 0, 1 or covered by AllHigh, plus failing triples for y-square, y-payload and large leading coefficients. It implements the executable check ltAllB and the partial decision decideSuccAff with soundness, failing witnesses and an exact description of the open class, total for unit successor. It classifies affine-multilinear and restricted-quadratic families and transports the unit decision to arbitrary signatures.
files.conclusion: Unit-successor root orientation of the free recursor is decided soundly and completely with failing witnesses, while larger slopes leave an explicitly mixed residual class.

files.summary: This file defines successor, wrapper and coupled recursor evaluations and the predicates for orienting the successor rule, zero rule and both rules. It proves alpha >= 1 and beta >= 2 sufficient for both rules with an explicit margin, and necessary by evaluating at zero and at payload beta+1. It generalizes to r-fold wrapper iteration with the exact threshold r <= alpha and r+1 <= beta, whose r=1 case is the main (1,2) construction.
files.conclusion: The coupled interpretation orients both free recursor rules iff alpha >= 1 and beta >= 2, with (1,2) as the minimal instance.

files.summary: This module turns each native reduction pair into a connector-aware chain reduction pair and proves that every actual pair-plus-connector chain step is strict and well-founded. It instantiates the theorem for the polynomial and gap-two pairs, whose strict relations differ. It gives a Boolean reset pair and connector showing that well-foundedness of the pair alone does not imply well-foundedness of the composed chain.
files.conclusion: Every native reduction pair certifies the full pair-plus-connector chain, while pair well-foundedness alone does not.

files.summary: This file defines calls, minimal chain steps, finite dependency-pair problems and the dpPairs relation, proving that finiteness gives termination and is monotone with an exact identity processor. It defines reduction triples and proves the triple processor sound, with a counterexample for swapped weak roles. It gives argument filtering, equational quotients and sharing simulations with exact cost preservation, each accompanied by controls showing deleting a live edge, quotienting the converse, or sharing without simulation is unsound.
files.conclusion: Finiteness of the dependency-pair problem implies termination and is preserved by reduction-triple, filtering, quotient and simulation processors whose side conditions are necessary.

files.summary: This file defines r-ary duplicating schemas with retention, integer counter gain and wrapper cost, proving orientation is exactly cost below gain. It shows retention forces gain above r copies plus cost, hence with uniformly bounded gain and unbounded payload no measure orients the rule at any r >= 1. It shows r >= 1 is necessary by an orienting arity-zero example, and identifies arity one with the binary P3.1 barrier.
files.conclusion: Retention plus bounded gain cannot orient the duplicating rule at any positive arity, and arity one is exactly the binary barrier.

files.summary: This file defines proof-bearing capstone structures ORI-1 through ORI-6, each field being the exact method-native row proposition from its implementation module. It proves each package closed from its native bundle and row anchors, without classifier equalities or True surrogates. It combines them with the generalized existing sixteen into a joint closure with exactly sixty complementary rows and preserved evidence.
files.conclusion: The six packages jointly close the sixty-row complementary wave plus the sixteen historical rows with typed evidence.

files.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for twenty conditional, typed, typing, graph, process and semantic rows on the free duplicating rule. Each escapable row exhibits a lens, a witness and a mutated value that keeps the row laws but loses acceptance, while inescapable rows prove laws determine the verdict with no separating feature change. It includes the barrier-premise linear-logic case and flat-wrap and heavy-share mutations for graph rows.
files.conclusion: Each row's characteristic law or data feature is necessary for acceptance, except where laws alone fix the verdict.

files.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for thirteen dependency-pair, usable-formative and substrate method rows for the free duplicating rule and related systems. Each row gets a necessity kind, a necessity statement on its own laws and acceptance predicate, and a proof by a concrete lawful accepted witness plus a feature change or deleted clause that preserves the remaining laws while losing acceptance. Three rows instead prove that the laws determine the verdict, so no feature change separates acceptance from rejection.
files.conclusion: Each of the thirteen dependency-pair, usable-formative and substrate rows satisfies its stated escape-feature, barrier-premise or laws-determine-verdict necessity property.

files.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for the fifteen interpretation rows, from linear polynomials over Q and R through max, nonlinear, multilinear, matrix, arctic, tropical, triangular, tuple, strict and extended algebras to finite models. Barrier rows delete one positivity, monotonicity, irreflexivity or finiteness clause and keep an accepted countermodel, while escape rows change one successor, recursor or strict-order feature. The arctic and tropical rows use a deleted wrapper-recursor pair with a covered split in which each part alone forces the contextual barrier.
files.conclusion: Each of the fifteen interpretation rows satisfies its stated deleted-barrier-premise or deleted-escape-feature necessity property, with the arctic and tropical rows additionally satisfying the covered two-part barrier with nonduplicating and contextual controls.

files.summary: This file proves hypothesis necessity for thirteen labelling, match-bound and sorted or constrained rows for the free recursor and schema. Escape rows change one labelling, system, position or order feature and lose orientation or the free-step adapter, while barrier rows delete height decrease or linearity and keep an accepted countermodel. Type introduction is a universal barrier rejecting the free recursor everywhere, and many-sorted and order-sorted rows have their verdicts fixed by the laws.
files.conclusion: Each of the thirteen labelling, match-bound, forward-closure, quasi-decreasingness, context-sensitive and sorted rows satisfies its stated escape-feature, barrier-premise, universal-barrier or laws-determine-verdict necessity property.

files.summary: This file states necessity for fifteen method rows for orientation closure. For barrier rows it shows a lawful witness exists, the duplicating rule is rejected at every datum, and a nonduplicating zero rule is oriented. For escape rows it shows a single feature change keeps laws but loses acceptance. For premise-deletion rows it exhibits a countermodel satisfying all other laws but violating the deleted clause while accepting.
files.conclusion: Every listed KBO, path-order and other-calculi row satisfies its stated barrier, escape-feature or fixed-verdict necessity.

files.summary: This file gives an executable decision procedure for the seven-constructor scalar direct-measure grammar. It implements positivity-at-unit and payload-dependence tests and proves them sound and complete. It proves counter sections are monotone and discretely convex, reducing strict response to the first increment. The classifier returns either a proof of orientation or a concrete failed duplicating-step instance, with evaluated controls.
files.conclusion: The classifier decides scalar orientation exactly, returning either an orientation proof or a concrete failed duplicating-step witness.

files.summary: This file defines the free first-order carrier for the two recursor rules. It introduces free terms, one-hole contexts with plugging, substitution and composition, and root and contextual rewriting. It proves substitution and context stability and packages the schema as an abstract step-duplicating system.
files.conclusion: Free terms and contexts with root and contextual steps form a substitution- and context-stable step-duplicating schema.

files.summary: This file supplies native semantic and structural witnesses for orientation method ORI-3. It builds a concrete extended monotone algebra, a weak one-point finite model, a raised match-bound certificate for countdown, and labelling and categorical controls. It proves linearity from raised certificates, the absence of any raised certificate for KO7, and the incompatibility of strict finite-model laws.
files.conclusion: Countdown admits a raised match-bound certificate implying linearity, while KO7 admits none and strict finite models are impossible.

files.summary: This file puts successor orientation for polynomial interpretations into separable form. It defines the separable difference and monomial-wise separable sum and proves orientation is exactly positivity of this difference over all bases, payloads and counters. It proves the zero-step necessity and zero-plus-step sufficiency and records the exact residual goal without claiming decidability, showing slope two admits both outcomes.
files.conclusion: Successor orientation on the open class is exactly separable positivity, which is two-sided at slope two and left as an exact residual goal.

files.summary: This file gives complete executable positivity decisions on two strata of the residual open branch. On base-affine and payload-affine signed polynomials it decides positivity by univariate checks with extracted failing pairs. It proves soundness, completeness and residual adapters and provides controls inside and outside the strata.
files.conclusion: Positivity on base-affine and payload-affine strata is completely decidable with extracted counterexamples, while biquadratic instances lie outside.

files.summary: This file defines the open residual instance interface and shows a total residual decider would decide zeros of signed bivariate polynomials. It gives a complete decision on the base-counter-monotone stratum via a payload-axis check with a finite coefficient certificate. It also gives complete decisions on payload-only and base-only univariate strata with failing witnesses and separating controls.
files.conclusion: A total residual decider would decide bivariate zeros, and the monotone and univariate strata are completely decidable with witnesses.

files.summary: This file embeds signed bivariate positivity into the slope-two residual branch. It defines natural and signed bivariate polynomials, their evaluation and squares, and the wrapper, lifting and encoding into recursor data. It proves the encoded residual equals the source polynomial and every encoding lies in the open branch, so the open class contains bivariate positivity and zero-existence.
files.conclusion: Slope-two residuals exactly encode signed bivariate positivity, so the open successor branch contains the full bivariate positivity problem.

files.summary: This file decides positivity for signed polynomials with one positive and one negative monomial. It proves the decision—positive constant dominating a smaller or vanishing negative constant—is sound and complete with extracted failing pairs and residual adapters. It supplies accept and reject controls outside earlier monotone and affine families and a decision table.
files.conclusion: One-versus-one monomial positivity is completely decidable by constant domination with explicit failing pairs.

files.summary: This file defines terms, substitution, one-hole contexts and the two recursor root rules over an arbitrary first-order signature with inert symbols. The free schema embeds injectively, its image is closed under root and contextual rewriting, and steps between embedded terms are exactly embedded free steps. The barrier cell and coupling inequality are transported to every signature schema. Strictly monotone inert operations plus root orientation give termination of the full contextual relation, proved by the coupled 1+sum polynomial.
files.conclusion: The recursor over every first-order signature terminates contextually via the coupled 1+sum polynomial interpretation.

files.summary: This file defines schema isomorphisms preserving base, succ, wrap and recur, with orientation of the duplicating rule transferring both ways. It identifies the free schema as the empty-inert instance and KO7 as the seven-symbol instance with integrate, merge and eqW inert, matching KO7 recursor rules to signature root steps. It characterizes the embedding image as inert-free terms and generated elements, proving agreement there but exhibiting distinct isomorphisms by variable renaming and by swapping merge with eqW.
files.conclusion: The free schema and KO7 are exact signature-schema instances with orientation transfer, unique on the generated fragment but not globally.

files.summary: This file defines size-change graphs of dependency pairs with strict subterm arcs and weak equality arcs, plus soundness of arcs as rewriting descent. It closes pair graphs under composition and states the criterion that every idempotent loop graph carry a strict self-arc. Using the infinite Ramsey theorem for pairs, the criterion implies well-founded minimal chains and termination under the variable condition. The system f(x) to f(x) fails the criterion with an infinite chain, while the free recursor satisfies it.
files.conclusion: The size-change criterion is sound for minimal chains and proves the free recursor terminating, while its absence permits looping.

files.summary: This module gives an exact executable extractor for the free recursor successor call with its source-target-call occurrence relation. It proves extraction exactness, strict decrease of a call rank, and well-foundedness of transformed calls. It then proves generic connector-aware chain soundness where strict pairs plus weak connectors yield well-founded chains, keeping source termination as a separate lexicographic bridge. A control with empty calls but a looping source shows pair well-foundedness alone does not imply source termination.
files.conclusion: Exact extraction and connector-aware chain soundness hold, but pair termination alone cannot serve as source termination.

files.summary: This module defines target-native ranks for graph, process and CPS carriers that strictly decrease on the existing lift steps, plus a generalized graph with an auxiliary weight. It introduces a finite replication-free pi fragment and a lambda-mu with CPS fragment, proving size-based termination and step-for-step simulation. A sharing-aware quasi-interpretation with strict contraction and a noninjective read-back control is proved. The exact transports and native arguments are assembled into the ORI-6 capstone package.
files.conclusion: Target-native ranks, fragment simulations and sharing contraction assemble into the ORI6 native-method package.

files.summary: Defines locally nameless System T terms with iterator It and recursor R and full reduction including beta and congruence rules. Defines the iterator fold from the free step-duplicating schema into System T and proves it is an injective closed embedding whose image is exactly the abstraction-, bound-variable- and recursor-free terms, transporting the exact orientation criterion, coupling inequality, barrier cell and four-cell verdicts and strong normalization to the image. Defines schema morphisms, characterizes maps out of the free schema as folds, and pulls non-barrier verdicts back along surjective morphisms and the image isomorphism. Proves no two-hole context realizes the recursor rule, gives the three-place wrapper with its coupling and barrier theorems, and defines two polynomial weights showing the free weight orients the iterator but fails on the recursor while a squared-counter weight orients both, yielding strong normalization of all abstraction-free terms.
files.conclusion: Every abstraction-free System T term is strongly normalizing under full System T reduction with iterator and recursor.

files.summary: Defines when a measure orients a relation and proves non-orientability persists under relation extension while well-foundedness persists under restriction. Defines renaming through an equivalence and proves it preserves and reflects termination, and defines positive simulations requiring a nonempty target path for each source step to transfer well-foundedness without injectivity. Gives a looping single-state source simulated by zero steps into an empty terminating target to show reflexive simulation does not transfer termination. Provides two deleted-premise controls: a zero-rule contextual relation oriented by term size that misses the duplicating root step, and a confluent fork-join source whose identity embedding reflects steps with closed image but drops joining steps so the target fork is not joinable.
files.conclusion: Positive simulations and bijective renamings transfer termination while reflexive zero-step simulations, root-missing contextual relations, and reflection without preservation do not.

files.summary: Restates the vector-order results for orientation: all-coordinate strict, genuine lexicographic, and strict-primary-weak comparisons each force payload-blindness of the relevant coordinates. Records that the two standard orders are well-founded while the PrimaryFirstLt compatibility relation is cyclic and ill-founded from dimension three, with counter-only vectors orienting both standard orders and payload-reading coordinates blocking orientation. Introduces the counter-then-payload vector that is lexicographically oriented while keeping payload in later coordinates, showing only the primary coordinate must be payload-blind, and notes matrix fixed-row and row-sum readings are scalar-dominated.
files.conclusion: Genuine lexicographic comparison orients the counter-then-payload vector, proving that orientation forces only the primary coordinate to be payload-blind while later coordinates may still read the payload.

files.summary: This file defines carriers for eleven path-order rows of the termination-method ledger, including KBO variants with status, quasi-precedence, AC matching, ordinal weights, applicative encoding and polynomial weights, plus equational and permutation RPO certificates and POP* and Cichon rows. It proves that every coefficient-weighted variable-condition order refuses the duplicating rule dupSrc to dupTgt because the payload variable count strictly increases, and that currying and AC rearrangement preserve those counts. It constructs the KO7 LPO and polynomial-rank escapes that orient all root rules and full-context closure, including a nontrivial AC-compatible order, a nonidentity permutation status, and the POP* impossibility and Cichon bound.
files.conclusion: No coefficient-weighted KBO variant or predicative POP* certificate orients the KO7 duplicating rule, while the KO7 LPO and polynomial rank yield nontrivial AC and permutation RPO certificates orienting all root and full-context steps.

files.summary: This file defines carriers for twelve semantic and structural rows, including extended monotone algebras, finite-model interpretations, linear-complexity certificates, three match-bound variants, four labelling policies with erasure, deterministic graph transports, relational categories, forward closures and quasi-decreasingness. It proves no finite carrier admits a strictly wrapper-increasing interpretation and no linear derivational-complexity certificate exists for KO7 by an exponential lower family, so match-bound certificates are empty. It proves every erasure-factored variable-condition comparator refuses labelled duplication while a constructor-sensitive root-label order orients it, is well-founded and transitive but not successor-context compatible. It proves deterministic graph transport is impossible by the equality fork while a terminating relational category containing that fork exists, and it records forward-closure right-linearity failure and quasi-decreasingness equivalence to strong normalization.
files.conclusion: Finite strictly wrapper-increasing interpretations and linear-complexity hence match-bound certificates are impossible for KO7, erasure-factored labelling stays blocked while a label-sensitive order escapes, and deterministic graph semantics is impossible although a terminating relational category containing the fork exists.

files.summary: This file defines the substrate-change predicates and seven escaping rows where the certificate lives on a new carrier with noninjective read-back, including shared term graphs, a merge-commutativity quotient, quasi-interpretations paired with a path order, and weighted type-graph, process and continuation carriers. It proves noninjective read-back alone with a Bool self-loop does not certify termination, while forward simulation into a well-founded target does. It proves the shared size orients duplication without factoring through read-back, merge commutativity identifies two distinct root-normal forms, quasi-interpretation axioms alone force no strict descent, and each graph, process and CPS lift exactly reflects KO7 root steps, decreases a rank, terminates and contains a foreign source outside the encoded image.
files.conclusion: Sharing, equational quotient and paired quasi-interpretation plus path order escape on new substrates, and the graph, process and continuation carriers each exactly reflect KO7 root steps, terminate by a decreasing rank, and strictly extend the encoded image.

files.summary: This file defines unary signatures, arity-preserving embeddings and maps, direct arity-preserving encodability, and the KO7 function symbols with their arities. It proves KO7 is not unary because merge has arity two and recDelta has arity three, and that no arity-preserving map or injective direct encoding exists from KO7 into any unary target signature. It concludes the direct unary-signature preconditions for cycle rewriting and string rewriting fail on KO7, without ruling out encodings that change arity or add auxiliary structure.
files.conclusion: KO7 is not unary and admits no arity-preserving map or injective direct encoding into any unary signature, so the direct unary preconditions for cycle and string rewriting fail.
